tagline: Wine worth the walk down the side street
sector: An independent fine wine merchant selling across the counter to retail customers and to restaurant buyers building by the glass lists.
founded_place_size: Established 2009, on a side street off the main shopping run in Edinburgh, Scotland. A small counter operation, one or two on the floor, an owner who buys the list himself.
about: Cellar & Cru is a merchant, not a shop that happens to sell wine. The owner tastes and chooses every line, and the selection changes with the season. When there is one of us on the floor and eleven people in, the shelf card is how a wine sells itself, so the card carries the grower, the region, the vintage, our note, the score and the price.
audience: Confident domestic drinkers and restaurant buyers aged 40 to 65 who read a shelf card the way a reader reads a review, and who treat visual noise as a signal about the wine behind it.
price_positioning: Independent fine wine. Bottles from 14 pounds to 220. The card is restrained and led by grower, region and vintage: generous white space, the score present but small, the price plain in the run of the line. Never the supermarket aisle, never fashion brand minimalism that hides the vintage.

palette.name: Cellar Ink
palette.usage: All type: the wine name, grower, region, vintage, style, buyer note and price, as talker_2025_PRINT.pdf sets them, and the wordmark. The key and vine device is this one solid ink, as it is printed in one ink on mark_card.jpg. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Claret
palette.usage: Only the short rule under the wine name, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never type, the price, a score, a ground or a panel.

palette.name: Vine
palette.usage: Optional. No supplied brand file gives it a role on the talker. If used, only as a small non-type accent, never type, the price, a score, a ground, a panel or any part of the key and vine device.

palette.name: Brass Key
palette.usage: Only the hairline under the wordmark, 0.2 mm thick and exactly 32 mm long, as the signature move sets it. Never type, a panel or a ring, and never a metallic or foil effect.

palette.name: Chalk White
palette.usage: The card ground throughout, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf, and the only ground or panel colour. Never type on the card.

palette.name: Stone Grey
palette.usage: Small labels, the score line, the picture keyline and the foot rule, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never the wine name, the buyer note, the price, a ground or a panel.

typography: Cellar & Cru runs two faces across four steps. Step 01 is the wine name in Eczar Regular 400 at 17 pt on 20 pt, tracking -0.01 em. Step 02 is the wordmark, CELLAR & CRU in Eczar Medium 500 caps at 7.5 pt on 10 pt tracked 0.30 em, fitted to a 32 mm measure above a Brass Key hairline 0.2 mm thick and 32 mm long, and set at 22 px on screen. Step 03 is the buyer's note, Eczar Regular 400 at 8.5 pt on 11.5 pt, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line. Step 04 is the fine print, Akzidenz-Grotesk Next Regular at 7 pt on 10 pt in letterspaced small caps tracked 0.12 em for region, vintage and score, with the price in the same face at 9 pt tabular lining, plain in the run of the line. The hairline and its 32 mm measure never scale with the type.
voice: Direct, measured and honest, the owner describing a wine as if standing beside you. It says what a wine is and is not, without hyperbole. Example: A co-op red that drinks well above its price, so long as you open it an hour before.
brand_assets_status: The original mark artwork went with the designer who moved abroad. The only clean version we hold is a photograph of the letterpressed compliments card he had made for us, carrying the mark at about 45mm. The autumn list, buyer's notes, scores and prices arrive from the till export.
values: A selection chosen by one buyer with a point of view, and a shop floor that sells wine honestly even when nobody is free to talk.

type_system.tagline: Wine worth the walk down the side street

scale.sample: Wine worth the walk down the side street
scale.note: The wine name. Flared cut serifs that read like a review. Existing size and leading kept exactly as the brand already sets them.

The wordmark, and the signature move. Point size is subordinate to the lockup: the line is always fitted to a 32 mm measure above a Brass Key hairline 0.2 mm thick and 32 mm long. Screen wordmark 22 px. The hairline never scales with the type.

scale.sample: A co-op red that drinks well above its price, so long as you open it an hour before.
scale.note: The buyer's note, set in the same face as the wine name directly beneath it. Maximum 65 characters a line. Existing size and leading kept.
Region, vintage and score. The price sets in the same face at 9 pt tabular lining, plain in the run of the line, never enlarged or emboldened.

type_system.signature_move: The wordmark is CELLAR & CRU in Eczar Medium 500 caps tracked 0.30 em, sitting above a Brass Key hairline that is always exactly 32 mm long and 0.2 mm thick. The lockup is fitted to that 32 mm measure at every size, so the point size follows the rule rather than the rule following the point size.
rules: The Brass Key hairline is always exactly 32 mm long and 0.2 mm thick, and never scales with the type.
The wordmark is always Eczar Medium 500 caps tracked 0.30 em, fitted to the 32 mm measure.
On screen the wordmark sets at 22 px.
The score is present but small, and the price stays plain in the run of the line: never colour, embolden or enlarge a price or a score.
Region, vintage, score and price are the only items in Akzidenz-Grotesk Next: 7 pt letterspaced small caps for words, 9 pt tabular lining for figures.
Never the supermarket aisle, and never fashion brand minimalism that hides the vintage: grower, region and vintage always lead the card.
Generous white space is part of the card, not a leftover.

palette_rules.distribution: Chalk White is the card ground and the only ground or panel colour, as on talker_2025_PRINT.pdf. On it, all type is Cellar Ink, the price included, as talker_2025_PRINT.pdf sets its wine name, record values, note and price; small labels and the score line may be Stone Grey. The key and vine device is Cellar Ink, printed in one ink as on mark_card.jpg. Brass Key is only the hairline under the wordmark. Claret is only the short rule under the wine name. Vine, if used, is only a small non-type accent. Stone Grey, Claret and Vine together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, the key and vine device is never a ghosted or transparent watermark, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a bottle photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, rules, keylines, the key and vine device or panels. No price or score is set in Claret, Vine or Brass Key or reversed out of a ring, badge or panel: the type rules never colour, embolden or enlarge a price or a score. No metallic, foil or gradient effect on any colour.
palette_rules.photography: Bottle photographs keep their own colour and are never tinted, duotoned or recoloured toward the palette: no bottle, label or wine is pushed toward Claret, Vine, Brass Key or Chalk White. Correcting a frame's white balance is allowed; restyling it is not.
